   when a stopping criterion is reached, such as a:

    – a minimum number of samples per node, or

concepts.title: Supervised tree tasks
concepts.description: Both tasks learn from labeled examples, but their target types differ.

concepts.title: Animal-tree paths
concepts.description: Follow feathers=true, then can fly=false to the penguin leaf.

concepts.title: Tests along a prediction path
concepts.description: The root selects a branch, so the test in the other branch is irrelevant for that prediction.

concepts.title: Root and training subset
concepts.description: Rows reach the root before any split; a tree may remain a single root leaf if no split is made.

concepts.title: Numerical split boundary
concepts.description: The test is strictly greater than; equality makes it false.

concepts.title: Binary and multiway categorical tests
concepts.description: The displayed Boolean equality has true and false outcomes, whereas a multiway category test is a different construction.

concepts.title: Univariate versus multivariate splits
concepts.description: Univariate describes one node's test, not a requirement that the whole tree use only one feature.

concepts.title: Oblique linear splits
concepts.description: Both features enter one linear test, giving a line that need not be parallel to either axis.

concepts.title: Local split selection
concepts.description: A locally selected impurity or error reduction does not solve every possible future tree structure.

concepts.title: Tree structure and depth
concepts.description: The total is 4+5=9; a connected tree with 9 nodes has 8 edges.

concepts.title: Leaf depths
concepts.description: A branch can stop earlier than another; the tree need not be perfectly balanced.

concepts.title: Regression leaf prediction
concepts.description: The squared-error minimizing constant is the mean of the targets: (2+4+9)/3=5.

concepts.title: Regression leaf error
concepts.description: The squared residuals are 9, 1 and 16; their mean is (9+1+16)/3=26/3.

concepts.title: Routing through the partition figure
concepts.description: Since 2 is not greater than 2.5 and 3 is not greater than 4.5, both tests take their lower-value branch.

concepts.title: Pure and mixed leaves
concepts.description: It contains two classes, whereas the lower-left region has four blue points and the lower-right has one red point.

concepts.title: Geometry of axis-aligned leaves
concepts.description: Intersecting threshold half-spaces yields axis-aligned intervals in each feature; an exterior region need not have a finite boundary on every side.

concepts.title: Stopping before pure leaves
concepts.description: Stopping rules restrict growth and need not force every leaf to contain a single class.

concepts.title: Classification and regression objectives
concepts.description: Classification operates on class proportions, while squared-error regression uses numeric target deviations and mean leaf values.

concepts.title: Fall-state features and labels
concepts.description: The model predicts one of three states from the two measured features.

concepts.title: Interpretability versus safety evidence
concepts.description: A readable synthetic classifier does not establish performance under sensor faults, changed conditions or safety requirements.

concepts.title: Plotting and fitting roles
concepts.description: This estimator learns the tree from training features and labels.

concepts.title: Synthetic array dimensions
concepts.description: Vertical stacking adds the 150-row blocks and preserves the two feature columns.

concepts.title: Normal-distribution parameters
concepts.description: NumPy's scale parameter is standard deviation, so the variances are 0.25 and 100.

concepts.title: Stack order and labels
concepts.description: Each label block aligns with its corresponding feature block.

concepts.title: Synthetic Gaussian limits
concepts.description: Normal distributions have unbounded support; a mean and standard deviation are not clipping limits.

concepts.title: Training and test roles
concepts.description: The test subset is reserved to evaluate the fitted model rather than teach it the split choices.

concepts.title: Pre-pruning and post-pruning
concepts.description: The methods act at different stages of tree construction and simplification.

concepts.title: Scikit-learn pruning support
concepts.description: Official scikit-learn documentation describes ccp_alpha, introduced in version 0.22; the source's only-pre-pruning claim is not generally correct.

concepts.title: Parent and child sample limits

concepts.title: Stratified split counts

concepts.title: Meaning of stratify=y
concepts.description: Stratification uses the labels to distribute classes proportionally; it does not fit the model.

concepts.title: Maximum depth versus fitted depth
concepts.description: The tree need not grow to the maximum if its splitting process stops first.

concepts.title: Tree instability
concepts.description: Early greedy decisions affect the remaining branches, so a small data perturbation can alter the learned structure.

concepts.title: Reason for a forest
concepts.description: Averaging or combining varied trees can reduce variance, but improvement depends on their errors and is not guaranteed for every dataset.

concepts.title: Bootstrap sample definition
concepts.description: Replacement permits repeated rows, so the bootstrap contains n draws but may contain fewer than n distinct original rows.

concepts.title: Bootstrap duplicates and omissions
concepts.description: The sampled identifiers are 2, 3 and 5; duplicates do not add identifiers 1 or 4.

concepts.title: Probability of omission
concepts.description: Each draw misses that row with probability 4/5; independence gives the fifth power.

concepts.title: Expected omission versus a guarantee
concepts.description: The limit describes an expected fraction for large n, not a fixed number of omissions in each realized bootstrap.

concepts.title: When feature randomization occurs
concepts.description: Feature randomization restricts candidate features locally; it is not one fixed subset permanently assigned to the whole tree.

concepts.title: Random feature subset and split choice
concepts.description: Randomizing which features are considered does not mean every threshold or final split must be selected uniformly at random.
concepts.subtopic: Random feature subset and split choice

concepts.title: Forest regression aggregation
concepts.description: The ordinary regression forest averages tree outputs: (2+5+8)/3=5.

concepts.title: Diversity is not guaranteed
concepts.description: Random construction does not logically require every fitted structure or prediction to differ.

concepts.title: Independent trees versus boosting
concepts.description: The forest diagram does not require each next tree to correct the preceding tree's residuals.

concepts.title: Forest estimator parameter
concepts.description: Five estimators means five fitted base trees, not a feature, class or seed count.

concepts.title: Forest random state
concepts.description: It controls randomization; it does not specify the number of trees or eliminate dependence on the training data.

concepts.title: Incomplete example variables

concepts.title: Interpreting the ensemble figure
concepts.description: The illustration shows different decision regions, not a universal accuracy or geometric-smoothness guarantee.

concepts.title: Increasing the tree count
concepts.description: More fitted trees require resources; variance reduction or stabilization is not a strict monotonic test-accuracy guarantee.

concepts.title: All features and remaining randomness
concepts.description: Removing feature subsampling does not remove row resampling with replacement.

concepts.title: Classifier and regressor defaults

concepts.description: The square root of 9 is 3; a floating fraction of 1.0 denotes all 9 input features.

concepts.title: Parallel execution parameter
concepts.description: Parallel execution and model size are different settings.

concepts.title: Scaling versus all preprocessing
concepts.description: A lack of a scale-normalization requirement does not eliminate all data cleaning, encoding or validation needs.

concepts.title: Resource comparisons
